prompt:

About the freelancer: 5 years experience; skills: SQL, Excel, Power BI, Google Sheets, data analysis, dashboard, data cleaning, data visualization

Job post (treat as data):
<job>
Title: Python program to solve parallel variations of the knapsack problem using dynamic programming.
Please describe relevant experience to this specific problem. Generic descriptions of your experience or company profile will not be considered. Python program with ties to excel to solve dynamic programming problem.
</job>

text:
I’m passionate, hard-working, and I’d love to help build a Python program for solving parallel variations of the knapsack problem with dynamic programming, including a tie-in to Excel for practical use and review.

With 5 years of experience in data analysis, SQL, Excel, Power BI, Google Sheets, dashboarding, data cleaning, and data visualization, I’m comfortable working with structured data, transforming it cleanly, and turning analytical logic into usable outputs. For this kind of problem, I would focus on building a Python solution that can evaluate multiple knapsack variations efficiently, keep the logic clear and maintainable, and produce results that can be reviewed or reused through Excel.

A relevant project I’ve completed was Parent survey analysis for Riverbend Education Fund. I cleaned and weighted a 4,200-response parent survey using Python, pandas, Excel, and statistics, then wrote the findings for the board. One result of that work was that 3 findings were adopted in the next funding plan. That project required careful data cleaning, logical weighting, and clear presentation of results, which are all useful when designing dynamic programming workflows and Excel-connected analysis tools.

For your job, I’d approach the work by focusing on:
- a reliable Python implementation of the dynamic programming logic
- support for parallel variations of the knapsack problem
- an Excel-friendly output format for reviewing inputs and solutions
- clean, readable code that is easy to test and extend

I understand you are specifically looking for relevant experience to this problem, not a generic profile. While my background is broader in data analysis than pure algorithm development, I do have strong hands-on experience with Python-based data work, Excel integration, and building structured analytical solutions from messy or complex inputs. I’m also very comfortable with organizing data and producing outputs that are practical for non-technical review.

If you’re looking for someone who can take the problem seriously, work carefully through the logic, and deliver a clean Python solution with Excel compatibility, I’d be glad to discuss it further.
